headline: Neemias Queta (rest) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Queta is back after sitting out Monday’s loss to the Magic, which was Boston’s second game in as many nights. His return likely pushes Luka Garza, who made a spot start and played 18 minutes against Orlando, to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Grizzlies announced on Tuesday that GG Jackson (foot) will be re-evaluated in three months.
body: Jackson suffered a broken fifth metatarsal in his right foot during Saturday’s win over the Nets. Tuesday’s surgical procedure was successful, and he’ll be re-evaluated in three months. Jerami Grant and Taylor Hendricks, who played 23 and 18 minutes, respectively, in Monday’s win over the Wizards, should absorb the minutes that would have gone to Jackson.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylin Williams (back) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Hawks.
body: Williams has missed Oklahoma City’s last seven games, leaving the Thunder to count mainly on Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara in the post. Mara’s minutes could decrease if JayWill returns, but he should still be in the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jock Landale (hip) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Landale’s continued absence means that Zuby Ejiofor should remain in the rotation, although he logged just 12 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Bucks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kingston Flemings (back) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Flemings will miss a second straight game with a back injury. With CJ McCollum (calf) out for at least four weeks, the Hawks will have to rely more on Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Jalen Johnson and even Dyson Daniels as on-ball playmakers. As for the empty spot in the starting lineup, Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins are two potential replacements.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes (illness) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Added to the Raptors’ injury report early Tuesday afternoon, Barnes will play despite being under the weather. Fantasy managers should make sure the star forward is in their active lineups before tip-off.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tobi Lawal (groin) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Due to right groin tightness, Lawal is trending toward not being available for Wednesday’s game. However, with Santi Aldama (ankle) on track to return, Lawal’s absence would not affect the Mavericks’ rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Walter Clayton Jr. (ankle) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Clayton, who played 23 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics, is dealing with a sprained right ankle. However, the probable tag suggests that he’s more likely to play on Wednesday than not. The Mavericks will have Kyrie Irving, and his availability limits Clayton’s ceiling, even if he remains in the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Max Christie (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Christie, who missed Dallas’ last two games, fully participated in Tuesday’s practice. If he can play on Wednesday, that may push Marcus Sasser out of the rotation after he logged 18 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Santi Aldama (ankle) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Aldama, who missed Sunday’s loss to the Celtics, fully participated in Tuesday’s practice. He’ll get minutes off the bench, likely pushing Tobi Lawal and Moussa Cissé out of the rotation entirely after they combined for 13 minutes on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes (illness) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Knicks.
body: Barnes is a late addition to the injury report due to an illness, which doesn’t bode well for his availability. If Barnes is sidelined, Collin Murray-Boyles could replace him in the starting five.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: According to the Pistons PR official X.com account, Duncan Robinson sustained a left quad strain in Saturday’s loss to the Heat, and he will be re-evaluated in a week.
body: Robinson’s absence should mean more run for Kevin Huerter, who has already seen a big boost in playing time and production across his last four games. Huerter is worth adding in all formats.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Aaron Gordon finished Monday’s loss to the Suns with 11 points (4-of-6 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), one rebound, one assist and two three-pointers.
body: Gordon scored in double figures on Monday, but the final line wasn’t anything special. Most disappointing may be the rebound output, as the Nuggets forward matched his season low in that category. Gordon is averaging 11.0 points per game, down more than five points from his 2025-26 average (16.2). While he remains rostered in 60 percent of Yahoo leagues, fantasy managers need to see more from Gordon. And soon.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Christian Braun accounted for 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Suns.
body: Braun has scored in double figures in three straight games, and he’s had at least one steal and one block in each. The stat lines haven’t been particularly impressive, but the ability to put something up in each fantasy-relevant category has given Braun’s value a boost recently. He’ll look to extend the double-digit points streak to four on Wednesday against the Celtics.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nikola Jokić accumulated 28 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 15 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Suns.
body: The good news for fantasy managers was that Jokić recorded a full stat line on Monday, finishing with his 10th double-double of the season. However, he also committed seven turnovers, matching his season high in that category. By Jokić’s standards, he started slowly, but the Nuggets’ center has remained one of the best players in fantasy basketball, regardless of league format.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jamal Murray finished Monday’s loss to the Suns with 28 points (9-of-19 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and one three-pointer.
body: Murray’s final stat line was boosted by a productive fourth quarter, as he shot 6-of-9 from the field and scored 18 points. That explosion helped the Nuggets guard avoid recording a poor stat line after a quiet first three quarters. And things won’t get any easier for Murray, as the Nuggets host the Celtics on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Miles Bridges recorded 16 points (7-of-15 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: While his numbers don’t jump off the page on most nights, Bridges’ consistency has made him a good player to have in category leagues. The Suns forward finished Monday’s victory with a full stat line, and he’s providing seventh-round value in nine-cat formats. Bridges’ fantasy ceiling may be limited, but the floor is safe.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dillon Brooks notched 15 points (6-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: After attempting two shots in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers, Brooks was far more active offensively on Monday. His 17 attempts led the Suns, and he scored 15 points for the second time in three games. At best, Brooks has been a late-round option for most of his career, with last season being an exception. Brooks is still rostered in 47 percent of Yahoo leagues, and Monday’s performance may have kept some managers from dropping him, despite the low field-goal percentage.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Green tallied 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, three steals and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: After struggling for most of the season, Green was efficient against the Nuggets. Shooting 50 percent from the field, he added value in multiple categories, including steals. Green’s three steals were a season high, bumping his total to 12 in 13 games. Even with the slow start, Green’s status as a starter is why he remains rostered in nearly 70 percent of Yahoo leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Devin Booker accounted for 20 points (5-of-14 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: After a brutal showing in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers, the Suns’ starters redeemed themselves on Monday. Booker didn’t shoot the ball well from the field, but the assist tally helped compensate for the low field-goal percentage. For the season, he’s shooting 47.3 percent from the field, so going 9-of-28 over the last two games hasn’t done much damage to Booker’s fantasy value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: LaMelo Ball struggled on Monday and finished with just six points (2-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers.
body: While it didn’t prevent Minnesota from getting the win, this was LaMelo’s worst game of the season. He set a new season low for points and failed to dish out an assist for the first time this season. This was an uncharacteristically bad performance for him, especially compared to what he’s done in the month of November. He was held to 19 points in their previous game, which was his first time scoring less than 20 points this month. He’ll get back on track in Tuesday’s rematch with Portland.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Rudy Gobert recorded a double-double on Monday with 18 points (5-of-10 FGs, 8-of-14 FTs), 15 rebounds, three assists and two blocks against the Trail Blazers.
body: This was the fourth time this season that Gobert hauled in at least 15 rebounds, but he hasn’t had a scoring performance like this one. He set a new season high for scoring and scored in double figures for just the fourth time this season. Gobert’s still effective on the glass, and while he has improved as of late, he isn’t the shot blocker he once was. However, a huge dip in both field goal percentage and free throw percentage have really tanked his value.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Javon Small amassed 12 points (6-of-11 FGs), five rebounds and 12 assists in Monday’s win over the Wizards.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Boozer finished Monday’s win over the Wizards with 29 points (10-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists and seven three-pointers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Patrick Williams (finger) will not return to Monday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Williams injured the fifth finger on his right hand, ending his night after playing 13 minutes off the bench. With Caleb Wilson (hand) out for multiple weeks, Williams’ role appeared likely to expand, but Monday’s injury could change that. Noah Essengue and Buddy Hield could see their minutes increase if Williams misses time.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bam Adebayo (hip) is questionable to return to Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Adebayo is dealing with tightness in his right hip and did not start the second half of Monday’s game. Andrew Wiggins, who shot 3-of-5 from three in the first half, replaced the Heat center in the starting lineup, which shifted Giannis Antetokounmpo to the five.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Carr (illness) is not on the injury report against the Hornets on Tuesday.
body: Carr missed Sunday’s game due to an illness, but he’ll be back to take on Charlotte. He may take on extra minutes with Austin Reaves (heel) sidelined, but it likely won’t be enough for him to make a big impact in the box score.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Walker Kessler (leg) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Kessler will miss Tuesday’s game due to a sore lower right leg. This is the first game this season the 7-footer has missed, and his absence has left a massive hole in the Lakers’ rotation. Sandro Mamukelashvili should see his role expand, and Kevon Looney could return to the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ryan Dunn (thumb) is available to play against the Spurs on Monday.
body: Dunn will be good to go despite initially being listed as questionable for this game. He’ll continue to play a significant role off the bench, though he hasn’t made a consistent impact in fantasy basketball.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Hayes will miss a second straight game after leaving Friday’s loss to the Rockets with a strained left knee. Mo Bamba, who shot 6-of-6 from three in Sunday’s loss to the Spurs, should get another start and is worth streaming until Utah’s frontcourt gets healthier.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves (heel) has been ruled out for Tuesday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Reaves will remain out for a second game due to this heel injury, and there isn’t a clear timeline as to how long he’ll end up being sidelined. Until he’s back, Quentin Grimes will continue to start, especially after he had 22 points and five triples in 37 minutes on Sunday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Amen Thompson (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Heat.
body: Sidelined due to a sore left knee, Thompson played 29 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Wizards. His absence frees up opportunities for Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard, with one likely moving into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: According to Tony Jones of The Athletic, Dominick Barlow (back) will be re-evaluated later this week.
body: Barlow suffered a lower-back stress reaction and has yet to appear in a game this season. If everything goes well with his re-evaluation, the power forward may be available for games soon. Given Philadelphia’s lack of depth at power forward and center, they’ll need Barlow to absorb some minutes once healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Luka Garza will start against the Magic on Monday.
body: With Neemias Queta getting a rest night, it will be Garza that steps into the starting lineup. Mitchell Robinson may take on a few extra minutes off the bench with Queta out, but it will be Garza that sees the biggest boost.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Isaac Okoro, Matas Buzelis and Jalen Smith will start Monday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Smith is good to go after missing Saturday’s win over the Timberwolves with a finger injury. He has reclaimed his spot in the starting lineup, and Zach Collins could fall out of the rotation entirely, since Nic Claxton is also available. The other four starters are unchanged, with Okoro continuing to start for the injured Caleb Wilson.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cam Spencer, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Monday’s game against the Wizards.
body: Edey is back after a two-game absence and will start, returning to his usual starting center role. However, the Grizzlies remain without Ty Jerome (hip), so Spencer starts again at point guard and is worth streaming.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane, Anthony Black, Franz Wagner and Wendell Carter Jr. will start Monday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Suggs, who returned from a knee injury on Friday against the Bucks, is back in the starting lineup for Monday’s game. As a result, Tristan da Silva will come off the bench. While his value takes a hit with the lineup change, da Silva is still worth holding onto since the Magic are without Paolo Banchero (ankle). The other four starters are unchanged.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Tyrese Proctor, Peyton Watson and Jarrett Allen will start Monday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Harden, Mitchell, Watson and Allen are back after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Mavericks, which was Cleveland’s second game in as many nights. Proctor, who recorded his first triple-double in the victory, will fill the void left by the injured Evan Mobley (toe) and can be streamed until the former Defensive Player of the Year returns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Amen Thompson (knee) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Heat.
body: Thompson is dealing with left knee soreness, and it could keep him sidelined for the second leg of a back-to-back set. If Thompson is ultimately ruled out, Tari Eason could replace him in the starting lineup, with more minutes available for Reed Sheppard.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) has been downgraded to doubtful for Monday’s matchup with the Bulls.
body: Tyson will miss his seventh game of the season, and that should open the door for Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor to take on expanded roles in a favorable matchup with Chicago’s lackluster defense.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: According to the Memphis Grizzlies PR official X.com account, GG Jackson suffered a broken left metatarsal in his right foot and will undergo surgery.
body: A timeline for Jackson’s return will be provided following the surgery. In Jackson’s absence, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant (head) should see additional playing time.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Domantas Sabonis produced 11 points (3-of-6 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds and three assists in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder.
body: Sabonis’ season-long fantasy value has been solid, with the Kings’ center providing top-50 per-game value. However, he has had a few rough performances. Sabonis recorded a double-double against the Thunder, but the shot attempts were surprisingly low on a night when the Kings were down Zach LaVine and De’Andre Hunter. Sabonis’ average of 8.8 field-goal attempts per game is his lowest since his rookie season (5.9 in 2016-17).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Malik Monk amassed 14 points (6-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder.
body: With Zach LaVine (illness) ruled out about an hour before tipoff, Monk made his first start of the season on Sunday. While he went 1-of-7 from beyond the arc, the Kings guard finished the loss with his first double-double of the season. The Kings don’t play again until Wednesday, which may be enough time for LaVine to get back. If so, there isn’t much to gain from rostering Monk in most leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Acuff Jr. finished Sunday’s loss to the Thunder with 26 points (10-of-25 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), one rebound, six assists and three three-pointers.
body: The good news for fantasy managers was that Acuff posted solid numbers in points and assists. Unfortunately, this was not a very efficient night for the rookie. Acuff recorded a season-high nine turnovers against the Thunder, which is far more damaging than the 40 percent shooting. Sacramento plays three games next week, starting with the Suns on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Aday Mara tallied 16 points (8-of-11 FGs), 13 rebounds and three assists in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
body: In addition to recording his third double-double, Mara established a new career high with 13 rebounds. While the rookie center didn’t record any defensive stats on Sunday, he’s emerged as a player worth rostering in some 12-team leagues. The only thing working against Mara in the short term is the schedule, as the Thunder won’t play again until Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jared McCain accounted for 12 points (3-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), one rebound, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
body: McCain has scored in double figures in six straight games, with Sunday’s being one of the few in which he struggled with his shot. The Thunder guard shot 1-of-8 from beyond the arc on Sunday, the first time McCain has failed to make multiple three-pointers in a game since November 4 against the Cavaliers. Limited production outside of points and three-pointers makes McCain more of a fantasy specialist than someone who can offer consistent value across the board.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ajay Mitchell (ankle) notched 14 points (6-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
body: After missing two games with a sprained ankle, Mitchell played 27 minutes against the Kings. The final stat line was solid, with the third-year guard doing everything but blocking a shot. Oklahoma City’s many injuries have put Mitchell in a position where he needs to be rostered in most leagues. And his skill set is such that maintaining top-100 value may not be too challenging.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Sunday’s win over the Kings with 37 points (13-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers.
body: In his final game of Week 4, Gilgeous-Alexander did whatever he wanted against the Kings. While shooting 65 percent from the field, the two-time MVP did not turn the ball over at all in 30 minutes of action. Oklahoma City’s blowout win meant Gilgeous-Alexander got some additional rest, as he did not play in the fourth quarter. SGA and the Thunder don’t play the first of their three Week 5 games until Wednesday. That isn’t great for fantasy managers, but it’s good for a team that’s been hit hard by injuries this season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nickeil Alexander-Walker delivered 20 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 33 minutes to lead the Hawks to a 113-106 win over the Bucks on Sunday.
body: Alexander-Walker has been an extremely consistent scoring threat, eclipsing 20 points on nine occasions this season. He’s offered a little bit of everything from a production standpoint, which has helped him grade out as an early-round fantasy contributor, averaging 21.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.5 steals and 0.4 blocks through 14 games. The Hawks are back in action with a three-game week that features tilts against the Thunder, Hornets and Pistons.
author: George Bissell

headline: Kasparas Jakučionis tallied a career-high 25 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and three steals in 26 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Hawks.
body: Jakučionis took advantage of his opportunity with Ryan Rollins out with an illness, hoisting a season-high 16 shot attempts and going 4-of-10 from three-point range. He’s played sparingly in his Bucks debut, but he’s shown that he can heat up and score in bunches when he’s given a chance. His role figures to expand once the Bucks begin to jettison some of their veteran pieces around midseason. Milwaukee has a three-game week on tap with matchups against the Heat, Trail Blazers and 76ers.
author: George Bissell

headline: CJ McCollum notched 20 points (5-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and four steals over 30 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Bucks.
body: McCollum stepped back into Atlanta’s starting lineup with dynamic rookie Kingston Flemings sitting out with a back strain. The elder statesman saved his best for crunch time, scoring eight of his 20 points in the final four minutes, including going a perfect 4-for-4 at the line during that span, helping the Hawks seal a narrow victory. The Hawks have a three-game week coming up with showdowns against the Thunder, Hornets and Pistons.
author: George Bissell

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns accounted for 28 points (10-of-21 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 17 rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Sunday’s game against the Kings.
body: Mitchell is back in the Thunder lineup after a two-game absence. However, instead of Williams, Aday Mara will head to the bench. The rookie center will remain in the rotation, but his fantasy ceiling takes a hit with the lineup change.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Andre Hunter (hip) is out for Sunday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Add Hunter’s name to the list of Kings contributors who won’t be available for Sunday’s game. With Precious Achiuwa also out, Leaky Black could move into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jayson Tatum accumulated 32 points (11-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals over 30 minutes to lead the Celtics to a 131-94 blowout win over the Mavericks on Sunday.
body: Tatum put together a feast-worthy stat line just in time for Thanksgiving, exploding for 21 third-quarter points to extend Boston’s lead to 33 and effectively put the game out of reach before the final period. It marked the 10th time he has scored at least 15 points in a quarter, the most in Celtics history since the play-by-play era began in 1996-97, just ahead of franchise legend Paul Pierce. He’s delivered second-round fantasy value, averaging 26.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, 7.3 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.8 blocks through 12 games this season. The Celtics have won six consecutive games and will kick off a busy four-game week against the Magic before heading out west to face the Nuggets, Clippers and Warriors.
author: George Bissell

headline: Cooper Flagg tallied 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 27 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: The Maine native did some real damage in the fourth quarter once the Celtics had already put the game away. It may have been garbage time, but it counts all the same for fantasy purposes. Simply put, Dallas looked like a completely different offense without primary initiator Kyrie Irving at point guard as he sat out the second night of a back-to-back in this one. The 19-year-old phenom has cooled off a bit over the last week, but he’s still averaging 23.5 points, 6.7 rebounds, 6.2 assists, 1.9 steals and 0.8 blocks through 13 games as one of the most impactful all-around contributors in fantasy. The Mavericks have a three-game week on tap that features showdowns against the Warriors, Clippers and Jazz.
author: George Bissell

headline: Derrick White notched 16 points (6-of-11 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and two steals over 23 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Mavericks.
body: White has been hot-and-cold from three-point range throughout his Celtics tenure, but he was locked-in during this contest, knocking down 4-of-9 from downtown. He didn’t end up with a block, but did come away with a pair of thefts as he was able to sit out nearly the entire second half as Boston built a massive lead, enabling them to cruise to the finish line. The Celtics have a four-game week on tap that includes showdowns against the Magic, Nuggets, Clippers and Warriors.
author: George Bissell

headline: Zaccharie Risacher delivered 18 points (8-of-9 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs) and five rebounds over 27 minutes in Sunday’s blowout loss to the Celtics.
body: Risacher was one of the few bright spots on an otherwise forgettable affair in Boston, as he saw huge minutes off the bench in a lopsided affair and was nearly perfect from the floor. His lone miss came from three-point range where he finished 1-of-2. The former top-overall pick from the 2024 NBA Draft fell out of favor in Atlanta, but he’s still young enough to envision a scenario where the change of scenery helps him turn things around. This effort certainly qualifies as a step in the right direction. The Mavericks have a three-game week coming up featuring contests against the Warriors, Clippers and Jazz.
author: George Bissell

headline: Zach LaVine (illness) is out for Sunday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Absent from the initial injury report, LaVine is now out for Sunday’s game. With De’Andre Hunter questionable and Precious Achiuwa out, the Kings could be extremely shorthanded. Malik Monk and Emanuel Sharp should see their minutes increase with LaVine out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is available for Sunday’s game against the Kings.
body: After a two-game absence, Mitchell is available for Sunday’s game. Kenrich Williams, who started Friday’s loss to the Clippers, could be asked to come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Quentin Grimes tallied 22 points (7-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and five three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Suns.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Suns with 43 points (13-of-28 FGs, 12-of-14 FTs), three rebounds, nine assists and five three-pointers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ousmane Dieng (finger) will undergo surgery on Monday and has no timeline for return.
body: Initially said to have suffered a sprained finger on his left hand, Dieng actually has a fracture that requires surgery. He’ll be out indefinitely, but this doesn’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ryan Rollins (illness) is out for Sunday’s game against the Hawks.
body: Rollins’ absence frees up minutes among the Bucks’ bench options. Kasparas Jakučionis, who did not play in Friday’s loss to the Magic, could re-enter the rotation with Rollins out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jock Landale (hip) is out for Sunday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Landale’s right hip will keep him out of Sunday’s game, leaving the Hawks light on options in the post. Zuby Ejiofor should slide into the backup center role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gui Santos (ankle) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: If there’s a positive to Santos appearing back on the Warriors’ injury report, it’s that his ankle is the issue and not a lingering knee issue. If he can’t play on Monday, the Warriors would have to rely a bit more on Georges Niang.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Chris Youngblood (foot) is out for Monday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Youngblood’s continued absence won’t impact fantasy basketball, but it does free up additional minutes for Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Steven Adams (calf) will start Sunday’s game against the Wizards.
body: Adams is available after missing time with a calf injury suffered during the Rockets’ season opener. With Washington starting Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr, Houston (which won’t have Fred VanVleet or Marcus Smart) will counter by starting Adams alongside Alperen Şengün. According to Rockets head coach Ime Udoka, Adams will play approximately 15 minutes. Joining Adams and Şengün in the starting lineup are Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant and Jabari Smith Jr.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Naji Marshall, Caleb Martin, Cooper Flagg, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Sunday’s game against the Celtics.
body: The Mavericks won’t have Kyrie Irving (knee) for Sunday’s game, which necessitates a change to the starting lineup. Marshall will fill the void, which also means even more on-ball playmaking opportunities for Flagg.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylen Clark (hamstring) will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
body: Injured during Saturday’s loss to the Bulls, Clark has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks. While he hasn’t been productive enough to be rostered in most fantasy leagues, Clark’s injury should free up additional minutes for Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon Jr.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome (hip) is out for Monday’s game against the Wizards.
body: Jerome will miss a second straight game due to a sore right hip. Cam Spencer played well in his absence on Saturday, recording 17 points, eight assists and three three-pointers. He is worth streaming in this spot, especially for managers needing assist production.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Michael Porter Jr. (personal) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Porter is back with the team after missing Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies for personal reasons. His return means that Noah Clowney will come off the bench after making a spot start against Memphis.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trendon Watford (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Watford’s continued absence won’t impact fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Monday’s game will be the fifth Murphy has missed due to patellar tendinopathy in both knees. Saddiq Bey has started the last two games and should remain in that role. He’s worth streaming, especially for managers needing points and three-pointers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bryce McGowens (elbow) is out for Monday’s game against the Warriors.
body: An elbow infection will result in a third straight absence for McGowens. His absence does not impact fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bennedict Mathurin (foot) is out for Monday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Mathurin will miss a second straight game after being a late addition to the Pelicans’ injury report ahead of Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets. He’s had a limited role when available, so his absence won’t impact fantasy basketball or the Pelicans’ rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Peyton Watson (hamstring) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Watson did not play in Saturday’s win over the Mavericks, leading to Mario Hezonja starting. If he remains out on Monday, Hezonja could get another start. However, the Cavaliers will have James Harden, Donovan Mitchell and Jarrett Allen available, which would limit Hezonja’s fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Tyson, who missed six games with a sprained ankle earlier this season before returning on Wednesday, started both games of the Cavaliers’ Friday/Saturday back-to-back. If he can’t play on Monday, the Cavaliers could turn to Meleek Thomas to fill the void in the starting lineup as they continue without Evan Mobley.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keegan Murray (illness) is available for Sunday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Murray is available to play after missing Saturday’s practice with an illness. He returned to the Kings’ starting lineup on Friday and should retain that role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Alex Sarr (illness) is available for Sunday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Sarr is good to go for Sunday’s game after initially being questionable with an illness. He’ll take on his usual role as the Wizards’ starting center, leaving Deandre Ayton on the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bub Carrington (chest) is available for Sunday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Carrington is good to go after a chest injury hastened his exit from Thursday’s loss to the Pistons. He’ll play rotation minutes off the bench, but Trae Young’s status as the Wizards’ starting point guard erases Carrington’s fantasy potential.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Adou Thiero (ankle) is available for Sunday’s game against the Suns.
body: Thiero has played rotation minutes since returning from a knee injury, and that should remain the case on Sunday. And there may be a few more minutes available with Austin Reaves (heel) sidelined.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Sexton (eye) is available for Sunday’s game against the Suns.
body: Sexton is good to go after initially being listed as questionable. With Austin Reaves (heel), Sexton should get additional minutes, even though he’ll likely come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bronny James (illness) is available for Sunday’s game against the Suns.
body: James hasn’t been in the Lakers’ rotation for most games. That’s unlikely to change on Sunday, even with Austin Reaves (heel) unavailable.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Aaron Fox (hip) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Fox was on the injury report ahead of Friday’s win over the Warriors with a hip injury, but he started and played 17 minutes. The Spurs’ point guard being added to the injury report late for Sunday’s game is a concern. If Fox can’t play, Julian Champagnie could move into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Morez Johnson Jr. (shin) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Johnson, who’s been playing through a left shin contusion, logged 15 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers. The rookie is likely to take on a similar workload on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving (knee) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Irving, who played 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers, played both games of Dallas’ most recent back-to-back on November 8-9. After playing 29 minutes in a win over the Nets, he played 39 minutes the following night against the Pacers. If Irving can’t play on Sunday, Walter Clayton Jr. will get more minutes, and Marcus Sasser could enter the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Daniel Gafford (shoulder) is probable for Sunday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Gafford exited Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers with a stinger, but he’s on track to play against the Celtics. If cleared, he’ll take on his usual role as the Mavericks’ starting center.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Quenton Jackson, Aaron Nesmith, Kelly Oubre Jr., Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac will start Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Already without Tyrese Haliburton, the Pacers won’t have Andrew Nembhard for Sunday’s game. As a result, Jackson moves into the starting lineup and will likely take on defending Tyrese Maxey. The other four starters are unchanged.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Steven Adams (calf) is available for Sunday’s game against the Wizards.
body: Sidelined since the Rockets’ season opener, Adams will be available on Sunday. He should slide into his usual backup center role, especially with Clint Capela (ankle) still out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ryan Rollins (illness) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Hawks.
body: Rollins is a late addition to the Bucks’ injury report. If he can’t play, more minutes become available to fellow reserve Kasparas Jakučionis, who was a DNP-CD for Friday’s loss to the Magic.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is available for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: McConnell’s playing time has increased by the game, with the veteran point guard most recently playing 17 minutes in Friday’s win over the Knicks. With Andrew Nembhard (hip) out, McConnell’s role has grown in importance. However, fantasy managers shouldn’t expect his playing time to increase much, if at all.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Aaron Nesmith (hand) is available for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Initially questionable, Nesmith sprained his left hand during the final seconds of Friday’s win over the Knicks. He’ll occupy his usual place in the starting lineup and could get more playmaking opportunities with Andrew Nembhard (hip) out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Andrew Nembhard (hip) is out for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Nembhard’s hip injury opens up a spot in the Pacers’ starting lineup. Quenton Jackson will start at point guard and is worth a look in deep leagues. T.J. McConnell, who logged 17 minutes in Friday’s win over the Knicks, is also available to fill the void left by Nembhard.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said that Jabari Walker will start at center for the injured Joel Embiid (foot) on Sunday against the Pacers.
body: Due to injury management reasons, Embiid will not play on Sunday. Walker has been tabbed to fill the void, making him worth considering for streaming. Nurse also said that LeBron James and Dean Wade should also see time at the five in smaller lineups.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Davion Mitchell posted a full line on Saturday with 15 points (4-of-7 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers against the Pistons.
body: Fresh off dropping a career high 17 assists on Friday, Mitchell wasn’t able to record another double-double, but he came close. He ended up making up for it by contributing extra value on the defensive end in what has been arguably his best two-game stretch of the season. He has been one of the best late-round picks in fantasy basketball this season and should continue to stuff the stat sheet as Miami’s starting point guard for the rest of the season.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 34 points (13-of-17 FGs), 14 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in a 137-117 win over the Pistons on Saturday.
body: Giannis wasn’t able to match his season high of 37 points that he set on Friday, but he was able to score at least 30 points for a third straight game, which led to Miami’s fourth straight win. Detroit didn’t have much of an answer for him, which helped him add an efficient shooting night to a dominant stat line. Plus, he was able to have an effective night at the free throw line, which helped inflate his value.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Klay Thompson returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed 26 points (10-of-17 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one block and six three-pointers against the Pistons.
body: Following a one-game absence, Thompson was back in the starting unit for the Heat and had another strong outing. This was his second-highest scoring performance of the year, and he has really shrugged off a slow start. Over his last seven games, he has averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 triples per game while shooting 50 percent from the floor and 46.8 percent from deep. If he continues to shoot this well, Miami should keep winning more games.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Duncan Robinson finished with 10 points (3-of-8 FGs), one rebound, one assist and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
body: Robinson exited this game late in the second quarter due to thigh soreness and didn’t end up returning. Kevin Huerter replaced him to start the second half, and if Robinson remains out in San Antonio on Tuesday, Huerter would likely get the start. Robinson has been a big part of Detroit’s success this season, but Huerter is a solid replacement that has been on fire lately.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 33 points (8-of-20 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a 137-117 loss to the Heat on Saturday.
body: It wasn’t a great encore after his performance on Thursday, but Cunningham still led the way for Detroit. 12 of his points came in the fourth quarter, though it wasn’t enough to complete a comeback. Cade has been effective from the free throw line all season, but he has been on fire lately. Over his last three games, he has shot 34-of-35 from the charity stripe. Unfortunately, he wasn’t quite as dominant as he was on Thursday. Still, Cade has been well worth the first-round pick.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kevin Huerter provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (9-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, seven assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
body: Huerter has been fantastic off the bench for Detroit lately, and he filled up the box score once again in this one. Over his last four games, he has averaged 16.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.3 steals, 2.3 blocks and 1.8 triples per game while shooting 54.2 percent from the floor. His role may continue to expand, as Duncan Robinson exited early with a thigh injury. If he ends up missing any time, Huerter would start in his place, just like he did in the second half of this game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Day’Ron Sharpe posted a double-double on Saturday with 16 points (7-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, five assists and one steal against the Grizzlies.
body: Sharpe started the year off slow, but he’s really starting to show why he was one of the best late-round targets. This was his second double-double of the season, and while he didn’t do as much on the defensive end in this game compared to what he’s done in recent games, he continues to be one of the best passing bigs in the league. Over his last five games, Sharpe has averaged 7.4 assists per game. Combined with efficient shooting, solid rebounding and defensive production, Sharpe’s game is tailor-made for category leagues.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Julius Randle led the Nets with 22 points (8-of-16 FGs), four rebounds, five assists, three steals and three three-pointers in a 129-110 loss to the Grizzlies on Saturday.
body: After three straight games scoring in the teens, Randle was finally able to get over the 20-point mark in this game. They needed his offense a little more than usual in this game with Michael Porter Jr. (personal) unavailable. It hasn’t been a great start to the season for Randle, but the volume will continue to be there for him. More nights like this one will help him improve his season-long numbers.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Noah Clowney started on Saturday and finished with 15 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, three assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Grizzlies.
body: With Michael Porter Jr. (personal) ruled out for this game late, Clowney ended up entering the starting unit. He took advantage of the opportunity and put together a solid stat line, complete with multiple blocks and triples. The Nets play again on Monday against the 76ers. If MPJ remains out, Clowney could be in line for another start and would have some streaming appeal.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Matas Buzelis delivered 18 points (5-of-9 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds and two assists over 30 minutes to propel the Bulls to a 117-106 win over the Timberwolves on Saturday.
body: Buzelis has gotten off to a rocky start overall this season, but he looked sharp in the early stages of this one, pouring in a game-high 14 points on 5-of-6 shooting, including 2-of-3 from beyond the arc, in the opening half. He cooled off considerably afterwards, notching just four points in the entire second half. Still, he managed to do enough as Chicago’s primary offensive creator in place of injured rookie sensation Caleb Wilson, who is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a fractured right hand, to power them to a much-needed road win. It’s hard to trust him for fantasy purposes given how up-and-down he’s been, but he should get plenty of scoring chances while Wilson is sidelined for at least the next month.
author: George Bissell

headline: Jaron Pierre Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, one steal, one block and two three-pointers against the Nuggets on Saturday.
body: After scoring 23 points for the Pelicans G League affiliate earlier in the day, Pierre ended up scoring in double figures for the second time in one day in this game. The 58th pick this past summer, this was the first time Pierre has played outside of blowouts, so it was good to see him play well. However, he shouldn’t be considered more than a dynasty stash at this point.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Tyrese Proctor recorded a triple-double with a team-high 24 points (10-of-19 FGs), 11 rebounds and 10 assists to lead the Cavaliers to a 127-117 win over the Mavericks on Saturday.
body: The Cavaliers were without their entire starting five on the second night of a back-to-back, with nationwide travel disruptions on Friday contributing to a lengthy list of absences. Donovan Mitchell (knee), James Harden (calf), Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jarrett Allen (knee) were all ruled out, while Evan Mobley missed his second consecutive game due to a toe sprain he sustained earlier this week. Proctor stepped up to lead Cleveland to an unexpected win by shooting over 50 percent from the floor, including 4-of-13 from three-point range. It was his first career triple-double. He’s played over 22 minutes in five consecutive games and has topped 15 points in three straight during that span. Cleveland has a three-game week coming up with home matchups against the Bulls, Grizzlies and Pacers.
author: George Bissell

headline: Kyrie Irving amassed a team-high 34 points (11-of-25 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block over 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
body: Irving was one of the few bright spots for Dallas in this one as they struggled to get anything going offensively until it was too late. The veteran point guard knocked down 7-of-16 from three-point range and fell just one point shy of matching his previous season-high, which he set earlier this week against the Pacers. He’s delivered second-round fantasy value this season, averaging 22.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.4 assists, 1.3 steals and 0.5 blocks through 11 games. The Mavericks are back in action with a quick turnaround when they face the Celtics, another one of Irving’s former teams, on Sunday.
author: George Bissell

headline: Thomas Bryant piled up a season-high 19 points (7-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds and three assists over 27 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Mavericks.
body: Bryant recorded a double-double after drawing the start at center with both Jarrett Allen (knee) and Evan Mobley (toe) both out of action. The 29-year-old big man has played sparingly this season, but could wind up seeing additional minutes off the bench if Mobley is out for an extended period. Cleveland has a three-game week coming up with home matchups against the Bulls, Grizzlies and Pacers.
author: George Bissell

headline: Cooper Flagg accumulated 18 points (6-of-19 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists and one block over 38 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
body: It was an extremely rare clunker for Flagg, who missed on all six of his attempts from three-point range and shot just 32 percent from the floor. He’s cobbled together a pair of lackluster performances following a season-high 43-point performance against the Pacers earlier this week. Despite the recent rough patch, he’s supplied first-round fantasy value as an all-around contributor this season, averaging 24.1 points, 7.0 rebounds, 6.4 assists, 2.0 steals and 0.8 blocks through 12 games. The Mavericks are back in action with a road tilt against the Celtics on Sunday.
author: George Bissell

headline: Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in a 116-108 loss to the Nuggets on Saturday.
body: Zion has taken major strides this season, and it has helped in fantasy hoops. Unfortunately, this was the third game this season that he failed to record a steal, which has been a strength for him, and he had his worst night at the free throw line this season, though he has improved overall this year. He made up for it by matching his season high for both three-pointers and blocks. Despite the lack of team success, Zion continues to fill up the box score.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Yves Missi returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed three points (1-of-4 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist and four blocks against the Nuggets.
body: Outside of the blocks, it wasn’t a great performance in his first game back. However, he was on a restriction that limited him to 22 minutes, and it was his first game since Oct. 23, which was a game he played just nine minutes. Basically, comparing it to his monster season-opening performance isn’t fair. Still, he immediately started, and he should keep that role moving forward. Keep holding on, and he should get better as he logs more games.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Christian Braun finished with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist, four steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Pelicans on Saturday.
body: After a rough 2025-26 campaign, Braun’s start to this season was rough. However, he has had some solid performances, and this was one of his best. His biggest improvement from last season has been on the defensive end, as he has been one of the best sources of steals so far this season. He hasn’t shot the ball as efficiently as he has in previous seasons, but he has made up for it on defense and will look to keep it going entering a four-game week.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jamal Murray lit up the Pelicans with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), seven rebounds, nine assists and two blocks on Saturday.
body: Murray has had an excellent season, but he has really picked things up over their last three games, averaging 30.3 points, 6.3 assists, 2.0 blocks and 3.0 triples per game while shooting 60.3 percent from the floor. He is averaging a block per game this season and has exactly two in three straight, but after averaging 0.4 swats per game last season, that mark will regress as the season continues. Still, it has been a fantastic start to the season for him, and with a four-game week coming up, he should continue to thrive for fantasy managers.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Nikola Jokić led the Nuggets with 26 points (9-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, three steals and one three-pointer in a 116-108 win over the Pelicans on Saturday.
body: It was a slow start to the year for Jokić, but he is starting to pick things up, especially over the last three games, where he has averaged 26.0 points, 11.7 rebounds and 9.0 assists per game while shooting 58.8 percent from the floor. The main improvement has been in his shooting percentage, as he is still at 51 percent on the season, which is well below his mark in recent years. This was the third time they’ve played the Pelicans this season, and while they did win all three, this was the only game where Jokić didn’t finish with a triple-double. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, they don’t play New Orleans again until April.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Austin Reaves (heel) has been ruled out against the Suns on Sunday.
body: Reaves exited early from Wednesday’s win, and he’ll remain out despite getting a few days off between games. Quentin Grimes will be back following a two-game absence and should get the starting nod with Reaves sidelined.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jerami Grant (head) has been ruled out against the Nets on Saturday.
body: Grant will be unavailable off the bench for Memphis in this game. He played 26 minutes on Friday and scored 26 minutes. They’ll likely turn to GG Jackson and Taylor Hendricks to make up for Grant’s absence.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Meleek Thomas, Tyrese Proctor, Jaylon Tyson, Mario Hezonja and Thomas Bryant will start against the Mavericks on Saturday.
body: The Cavs played in Miami on Friday and then had flight delays (like everyone did) that prevented them from returning to Cleveland when they intended. So they’re resting the entire starting five. It will be five new starters for the Cavs, though they will all likely return to reserve roles in their next game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Michael Porter Jr. (personal) has been ruled out against the Grizzlies on Saturday.
body: MPJ was a very late addition to the injury report, and he will now be unavailable against Memphis. Chaney Johnson and Terance Mann are both candidates to replace him in the starting unit, though Danny Wolf could continue to start despite Nolan Traore’s return in place of MPJ.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) has been ruled out against the Spurs on Sunday.
body: Hayes exited early from Friday’s game against Houston, and he will remain out against San Antonio. Jusuf Nurkić is still out, which means Mo Bamba should start at center, with Kyle Filipowski filling out extra minutes off the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jeremiah Fears, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey, Zion Williamson and Yves Missi will start against the Nuggets on Saturday.
body: Missi will start in his return to the lineup following an 11-game absence. His return will push DeAndre Jordan out of the starting unit and likely out of the rotation altogether. Missi will be on a minutes restriction, so Derik Queen and Karlo Matković should see a few extra minutes.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Norman Powell (back) is available to play against the Pistons on Saturday.
body: Powell will be good to go on the second night of Chicago’s back-to-back. He was questionable initially due to a back injury that caused him to miss two games this past week. He scored 33 points on Friday and will look to stay hot in this one.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jalen Smith (finger) has been ruled out against the Timberwolves on Saturday.
body: Smith will be sidelined for the second leg of this back-to-back, and Nic Claxton will be as well. Zach Collins should start at center, with Orlando Robinson filling out the backup minutes down low.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Nic Claxton (hamstring) has been ruled out against the Timberwolves on Saturday.
body: Claxton will be unavailable for this game, which is the second leg of a back-to-back. Jalen Smith is out as well, so Zach Collins and Orlando Robinson should fill out the center minutes.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Nolan Traoré (calf) is available to play against the Grizzlies on Saturday.
body: Traoré will be back following a one-game absence. Danny Wolf will likely head back to the bench, though he could remain a starter if Michael Porter Jr. (personal) ends up missing this game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Klay Thompson (ankle) is available to play against the Pistons on Saturday.
body: Thompson will be back following a one-game absence. Tim Hardaway Jr. started in his place on Friday, with Ryan Conwell also seeing a big bump in minutes off the bench. THJ will likely be bumped out of the rotation, with Conwell playing a smaller role.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo (ankle) is available to play against the Pistons on Saturday.
body: Giannis is still managing a wrist injury, which had him initially listed as probable. He’ll be good to go and will look to stay hot after scoring 37 points in Friday’s win over the Cavaliers.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Mikel Brown Jr. (illness) is available to play against the Grizzlies on Saturday.
body: Brown will be good to go, as expected. However, Michael Porter Jr. has been added to the injury report as questionable due to personal reason. This is less than two hours before tipoff, which could open the door for either Chaney Johnson or Terance Mann to start.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kingston Flemings (back) has been ruled out against the Bucks on Sunday.
body: Flemings exited early from Friday’s game, and that same lumbar strain will keep him out against Milwaukee. CJ McCollum should return to the starting unit with Flemings unavailable.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Austin Reaves (heel) missed practice on Saturday.
body: Reaves is dealing with a heel bruise. The 28-year-old guard missed practice Saturday, though it’s unclear if he’ll miss any game time.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jerami Grant (head) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Nets.
body: Grant scored 22 points in 26 minutes off the bench Friday against the Pelicans, but is listed as questionable with a head injury Saturday against the Nets. If he’s ruled out, GG Jackson could see a minutes bump.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Ty Jerome (hip) is out for Saturday’s game against the Nets.
body: Jerome is out with right hip soreness. Cam Spencer could move into the starting lineup in Jerome’s absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Peyton Watson (hamstring) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Watson is on the crowded Cavaliers injury report as questionable with right hamstring injury management. Cleveland’s rotation is truly up in the air until we have more clarity on some of these injury situations.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jarrett Allen (knee) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Allen has a knee injury and is questionable on the injury report, where he has plenty of company from Cavaliers teammates. Ideally, Allen would start, but if he’s ruled out along with Evan Mobley, who has already been ruled out, Thomas Bryant could be in line to start.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Evan Mobley (toe) and Sam Merrill (elbow) are out for Saturday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Mobley will miss his second game in a row with a left great toe sprain. Merrill will also be out again with right elbow injury management. Without the two, Cleveland can play small with Peyton Watson or use Meleek Thomas and Jaylon Tyson off the bench.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: James Harden (calf) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Harden had 20 points in 35 minutes in the loss against the Heat Friday. He’s listed as questionable with a calf injury for Saturday’s game against the Mavericks. If he’s out, Tyrese Proctor could move into the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Donovan Mitchell (knee) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Mitchell is listed as questionable with left knee injury management. Given the Cavaliers’ crowded injury report, Tyrese Proctor and Craig Porter Jr. could see more minutes Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Klay Thompson (ankle) is probable for Saturday’s game against the Pistons.
body: Thompson missed Friday’s game against the Cavaliers, but is likely to return Saturday given his probable listing. With Pelle Larsson (illness) doubtful, Thompson could see a lot of minutes if he’s available.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Aday Mara recorded 10 points (5-of-6 FGs), three rebounds and three blocks in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: While Mara has started four of Oklahoma City’s last six games, the 21 minutes he logged on Friday were the least he’s played in any of those starts. There were some positives to the rookie’s performance, specifically the field-goal percentage and blocked shots. However, Mara hasn’t done enough with Chet Holmgren (knee) out to become a player who has to be rostered in 12-team leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Hartenstein notched 21 points (9-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 16 rebounds, six assists and one steal in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: After scoring no more than seven points in any of Oklahoma City’s first five games in November, Hartenstein has scored at least 20 in two straight games. He was outstanding against the Clippers, shooting 90 percent from the field and providing excellent value in points, rebounds and assists. Providing top-100 fantasy value, Hartenstein is rostered in 84 percent of Yahoo leagues. Given Oklahoma City’s frontcourt injuries, those rostering Hartenstein would be better served holding on to him than entertaining a trade after the last two games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jared McCain tallied 23 points (8-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: McCain has scored in double figures in four straight games, with Friday’s being the best of the bunch. The Thunder guard shot 7-of-11 from deep against the Clippers, recording season highs in points and three-pointers. McCain will mainly be a “points and triples” option in fantasy leagues, but Oklahoma City’s injuries open the door for him to provide consistent value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
body: Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keaton Wagler produced 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
body: After reaching double figures in each of his first five games, Wagler totaled 13 points on 4-of-13 shooting in the Clippers’ first two games of November. The rookie has gotten back on track, having scored at least 11 points in four straight games. Wagler remains a deep-league option in redraft formats, while dynasty league managers should be excited for the rookie guard’s future.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, one steal, four blocks and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
body: Thanks mainly to the three-pointers and defensive stats, Jones has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. Against the Thunder, he shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and recorded five “stocks” in 29 minutes. This was Jones’ fourth game this season with at least two three-pointers, one steal and one block. Managers needing help in those categories should consider adding Jones ahead of Sunday’s game against the Hornets.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
body: After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
body: After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Domantas Sabonis put up 21 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, and a three in the loss on Friday to the Blazers.
body: After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Darius Acuff scores 17 points (6-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals, and three 3-pointers in 120-107 loss to the Blazers.
body: Acuff got going in the second half after a bad start. He adjusted to how Portland was guarding him and he started hitting more of his shots. He helped spearhead the comeback late in the fourth after being down 20. He’s getting better each game and is still being one of the best scorers in the NBA this season.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama will start Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: After a two-game absence, Vassell is available for Friday’s game. His return means that Julian Champagnie will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson Julian Champagnie

headline: The Warriors will start Brandin Podziemski, Will Richard, De’Anthony Melton, Yaxel Lendeborg, and Draymond Green against the Spurs on Friday.
body: Steph Curry suffered a right oblique abdominal tear and will be out for tonight’s game. The Warriors made two changes to the starting lineup, first with sliding Draymond Green to the five and replacing Al Horford with Will Richard, and then De’Anthony Melton will start in place of Steph Curry. Richard isn’t a great fantasy player, but Melton is the guy to add if he’s available in your fantasy league.
author: Brian Taylor De'Anthony Melton Will Richard
